name: GigaBASE
tagline: Knizhnik's embedded object-relational DBMS for C++ with a page pool, SubSQL and R-tree indexes.
description: GigaBASE is an embedded object-relational database by Konstantin Knizhnik, the disk-oriented sibling of his main-memory FastDB. Where FastDB maps the whole file into memory, GigaBASE reads pages through a buffer pool, so databases can be far larger than RAM. C++ classes are described with macros and the schema is derived and evolved automatically; queries use SubSQL, a SQL-like language with direct object references, arrays, B-tree, R-tree and time-series support, and transactions use shadow paging, so there is no log and recovery is instant. APIs exist for C, C++, C#, Java, PHP and Perl. The last release, 3.91, shipped in May 2014 under an MIT-style license; it still compiles for embedded C++ use but is unmaintained.
statusNote: No release since 3.91 (May 2014); the code remains downloadable from garret.ru and SourceForge but is unmaintained.

scale.notes: Single-file databases up to the terabyte range on one machine; optional replication to a standby.

strengths: Tight C++ integration with automatic schema derivation and evolution
Shadow-page transactions: no write-ahead log and instant recovery
B-tree, R-tree and time-series data types in a small embeddable library
Direct object references avoid join overhead for navigational access
weaknesses: Small user base and dated documentation
Single-writer concurrency model limits write-heavy multithreaded use
useCases: Embedded C++ applications that need an object-relational store
Maintaining legacy software built on GigaBASE
notIdealFor: New projects needing an active community
